message:
refactor(host): put the kill behind a seam a test can replace

Product 3 (one split into two TUs plus a header), test 1, build 1. No behaviour change: the
shipping path does exactly what it did.

The branch for "the helper would not die" is untested and cannot honestly be tested, because
TerminateProcess does not fail for a process we started. Removing the branch breaks nothing, which
is another way of saying nothing covers it. The reviewer's answer is the right one: replace the OS
call, not the product logic.

So terminate-and-confirm is its own translation unit now. The product links
host_thumbnail_kill.cpp; a lingering test will link host_thumbnail_kill_fault.cpp, which does not
terminate and reports failure -- driving the real teardown down the real path with a helper that is
genuinely still running. Link-time rather than a flag, deliberately: a runtime switch would mean
the shipping binary contains a way to make its own kill fail, and then the interesting question
becomes whether production can reach it.

The gate checks that it cannot. GNLinkStream is read as well as GNLinkCapture -- the host is where
the kill is linked, so it is the only place the fault file could land -- and a marker string from
that file is now on the forbidden list.

That check was worthless when first written, and the mutation is what said so. The marker was a
namespace-scope constant nobody referenced, so the linker dropped it: linking the fault TU into the
product on purpose still passed the gate. A check that cannot fail is not a check. It is written
through a volatile pointer now, and the same mutation fails the gate as it should. Reverted, 19 of
19.

Which is the third time in this task that a scan needed proof it could find anything before its
silence meant something. The existing positive controls cover the helper's own switches and did not
extend to a string I added later.
